codeReview.summary: The rerun fix adequately resolves the prior VAL-CROSS-003 blockers. Compared with the failed `dbeba84c5b9abd0e1350708e84ca9234ac270f89` diff, commit `a8e6527` removes the mirrored `TestableRuntimeObservingHost`, adds a real-host setup helper plus four end-to-end resize/DPI assertions in `Tests/SwiftWindowsCoreLogicTests/WinSwiftUIWindowHostTests.swift:201-223` and `405-500`, and updates `WinSwiftUIWindowHost.window(_:didResizeTo:)` to carry the live `window.scaleFactor` into the cached surface descriptor before renderer resize/fallback in `Sources/WinSwiftUI/App.swift:245-250`. The new tests now drive the production `WinSwiftUIWindowHost` seam, use `window.scaleFactor` rather than a test-only surface-descriptor DPI path, and prove the same-session fallback path reattaches, resizes, activates, and renders through the frame backend after batch resize failure.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Windows worker bootstrap still has a tooling gap: `.factory/init.sh` is a bash shim even on this Windows-only mission, so the worker had to bypass the documented init step and use `.factory/windows-swift-env.ps1` directly.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `.factory/init.sh:1-5` is a bash wrapper over `windows-swift-env.ps1 -CheckOnly`; the `1dc25800-7ebd-456f-9061-e7ef2ffe7174` transcript skeleton shows attempts to run `.factory/init.sh` and then `bash ...init.sh`, and the handoff `skillFeedback` records that no WSL/bash distribution was available so the worker switched to the PowerShell command directly.

summary: Pass: the round-two fix closes the prior VAL-CROSS-003 scrutiny blockers by proving resize and DPI propagation through the real `WinSwiftUIWindowHost` seam and by validating the real same-session frame-fallback resize path.
